evals.name: split-vague-dashboard
evals.prompt: split this task: build the caregiver dashboard so a parent's medication reminders show up for the whole family
evals.expected_output: The original fails several letters; it is split into small slices a person can use, in build order; Story 1 is written in full; it stops for approval.
assertions: Grades all six letters (Independent, Negotiable, Valuable, Estimable, Small, Testable) pass or fail, with a reason for each fail
Every piece it proposes is sized at 2 weeks or less
Story 1 uses the formula: As a [audience], I want [goal], so that [value]
Story 1 has acceptance criteria and at least one Given/When Then scenario
Describes outcomes and does not prescribe screens, tools or code
Ends with a receipt (Audited, Split, Written, Not checked)
Stops after Story 1 and asks for approval before Story 2
scripts/check_invest.py passes on the answer (run on the saved text)

evals.name: audit-already-good-story
evals.prompt: Audit this user story with INVEST: As an adult child caring for a parent, I want to ask a sibling to cover one evening, so that I can take a break without calling everyone. It takes about a week.
evals.expected_output: Passes most letters, is not over-split, notes anything weak (for example how a sibling answers), and still ends with a receipt.
assertions: Grades all six letters
Does not split a story that already passes Small
Ends with a receipt
Stops and waits for the owner

evals.name: rewrite-solution-shaped-story
evals.prompt: user story: As a user, I want a dropdown menu in the sidebar with a red Remind button, so that I can click it.
evals.expected_output: Flags that it names a solution and has no benefit; rewrites it as an outcome for a named audience.
assertions: Fails Negotiable and says why (dropdown, sidebar and button are solutions)
Rewrites the story as an outcome for a named audience
Does not keep the dropdown or button in the rewritten story

evals.name: scope-the-whole-app
evals.prompt: let's use INVEST to scope the whole caregiver app for the MVP
evals.expected_output: Says this is far too big; proposes epics and features, not 40 tickets; asks before generating a long list.
assertions: Fails Small and Independent for the whole app
Asks before producing a long list (more than about 9 pieces)
Does not write dozens of full stories at once

evals.name: homework-deliverable
evals.prompt: scope the feature analysis deliverable with INVEST. It is a homework analysis table, not code.
evals.expected_output: Uses homework mode or asks which mode; grades and splits the deliverable into checkable steps with a definition of done; no forced 'As a user' sentence.
assertions: Uses homework mode or asks the owner which mode to use
Gives a definition of done and checks for each step
Does not force an app-feature story sentence onto an analysis

evals.name: tiny-fix-should-not-trigger
evals.prompt: fix the typo in the README heading
assertions: The invest-task-scoping skill is not used
